title: JavaScript Fundamentals
description: Closures, event loop, async/await, this binding, prototypes, type coercion, floats, ES6+ APIs. Tested on every Turing MCQ, Andela pair-programming, Toptal live coding, and FDE coding rounds.

questions.code:
console.log(a);
var a = 1;
questions.explanation: `var` declarations are hoisted and initialized to `undefined`. The assignment stays in place.

questions.code:
console.log(a);
let a = 1;
questions.explanation: `let`/`const` are hoisted but sit in the Temporal Dead Zone until the declaration is reached. Access before that throws ReferenceError.
`var i` is function-scoped, so all three callbacks share the same `i`. By the time the timers fire, the loop has finished and `i === 3`. Replace `var` with `let` for `0 1 2`.
`let` creates a fresh binding per iteration, so each closure captures its own `i`.
Sync first (A, D). Microtasks (Promise.then) run before the next macrotask, so C prints. Then the setTimeout callback prints B.
1 prints synchronously. `await null` schedules the rest as a microtask, so 3 prints before 2.
`==` coerces: '0' → 0, false → 0. `===` requires same type. `NaN` is never equal to itself.

questions.prompt: Which of these evaluate to `false`? (select all)
questions.explanation: Falsy values in JS: `false, 0, -0, 0n, '', null, undefined, NaN`. Empty array and object are truthy. Non-empty string '0' is truthy.
Detaching the method loses the receiver. In non-strict, `this` becomes globalThis (no `x`), so `undefined`. In strict mode, `this` is `undefined` and access throws TypeError.
Arrow functions do NOT have their own `this`. They inherit from the enclosing lexical scope (globalThis at top level), which has no `x`.
IEEE 754 floating-point: 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004. Use `Math.abs(a-b) < Number.EPSILON` for float equality.
Each `counter()` call creates a fresh `c`. `a` called 4 times → 4. `b` called once → 1.
Array literals inherit from Array.prototype, which itself inherits from Object.prototype.

questions.code:
Promise.resolve(1)
  .then(v => v + 1)
  .then(v => { throw new Error('x') })
  .then(v => v + 1)
  .catch(e => console.log(e.message))
  .then(() => console.log('done'));
questions.explanation: The thrown error skips subsequent `.then`s until `.catch`, which logs 'x'. The final `.then` after `.catch` still runs → 'done'.
`main()` runs sync until `await`. `sync` logs. Then microtask runs, catches, logs 'caught err', then 'after'.

questions.prompt: Which Array methods MUTATE the original array? (select all)
questions.explanation: sort, splice, reverse, push, pop, shift, unshift, fill, copyWithin all mutate. map/slice/concat/filter/reduce return new arrays.
Spread flattens each array into elements: [1,2,3,4,5], length 5.

questions.code:
const { a = 1, b = 2 } = { a: undefined, b: null };
console.log(a, b);
questions.explanation: Default values apply ONLY when the source is `undefined`, not `null`. So `a` becomes 1, but `b` stays `null`.
`for...in` iterates enumerable string keys, including non-index properties. Use `for...of` for values or `arr.forEach` for indices only.
`b = a` copies the reference (both point to same object). Mutating via `b` changes `a`. Spread creates a shallow copy → `c` is independent.
Spread is a SHALLOW copy. `nested` is still shared by reference. Use `structuredClone(a)` for deep copy.
`let` is block-scoped. Inner `x` shadows outer inside the block only.

questions.prompt: Which is TRUE about ES modules (ESM)?

options.text: Imports are hoisted and evaluated once, then cached

questions.explanation: ESM: imports hoisted + singleton-cached. `this` is `undefined` at top level. `require` is CJS. Top-level `await` is allowed in ESM.

questions.prompt: In what order do these log?
questions.explanation: Order (Node.js): sync → nextTick queue → microtasks (Promises) → macrotasks (timers, then immediates). t1/i1 order depends on context but usually t1 first when scheduled from main.
`await` inside `for...of` runs sequentially. For parallelism use `Promise.all(arr.map(async ...))`.

questions.prompt: Which correctly runs N async ops in parallel and waits for all?

options.text: for (const x of xs) await fn(x)

questions.explanation: `Promise.all` collects promises and awaits them concurrently. forEach ignores returned promises. Awaiting a mapped array of promises directly doesn't work — `.map(fn)` returns an array, not a promise.
Generator yields 1, 2, then `return 3` produces {value:3, done:true} and stops. Further next() returns {value:undefined, done:true}.

questions.prompt: Which statement about `Map` vs plain object is FALSE?

options.text: Map keys can be any type, including objects
Map is slower than plain object for all operations

questions.explanation: Map is often faster for frequent add/remove, and always faster to get size. Objects have prototype-key pitfalls Map avoids.

questions.code:
const s = new Set([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3]);
console.log(s.size, [...s].join(','));
questions.explanation: Set dedupes on insertion. `size` is a property (not method). Spread preserves insertion order.
Classic closure bug. `var i` is shared. Fix with `let i` or IIFE.

questions.prompt: Which correctly handles a fetch that must retry up to 3 times on network failure?

options.text: async function retry() { for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { try { return await fetch(url); } catch (e) { if (i === 2) throw e; } } }

questions.explanation: Sequential retry with return-on-success and rethrow-on-final-failure. Add exp backoff for production.

questions.code: console.log(typeof null, typeof [], typeof NaN, typeof undefined);
questions.explanation: `typeof null === 'object'` (historical bug), arrays are objects, `NaN` is a number. Use Array.isArray to detect arrays.

questions.prompt: Given `class B extends A`, which is the correct super constructor call in B's constructor?
questions.explanation: In class syntax, `super()` must be called before `this` is used in a subclass constructor.

options.text: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined

questions.explanation: Regular function in setInterval loses `this`. In strict mode → TypeError. In non-strict → `this` is globalThis, so it silently adds `n` there without affecting the Timer. Fix: arrow fn or bind.

questions.prompt: Which correctly return a new array without mutating the original? (select all)
questions.explanation: splice mutates. Others return new arrays. `toReversed`/`toSorted`/`toSpliced`/`with` are ES2023 immutable-array methods.

questions.code:
async function f() { console.log('x'); }
await Promise.all([f(), f(), f()]);

options.text: SyntaxError unless in a module or async fn

questions.explanation: Top-level await only works in ES modules or inside an async function. Otherwise: SyntaxError.

questions.prompt: Which regex matches a valid email (basic form) at start-to-end?
questions.explanation: Basic email = something + @ + domain + . + tld, anchored. Full RFC-compliant regex is much longer.
Classic groupBy via reduce. Odd bucket: 1,3. Even bucket: 2,4. (ES2024 adds `Object.groupBy` natively.)

questions.prompt: Where does the error get caught?

options.text: The error is uncaught (crashes or bubbles to global)

questions.explanation: try/catch only wraps SYNCHRONOUS code. The callback runs later on a different call stack — the outer try is long gone. Handle inside the callback or use async/await.
SHARED cache object across all memoized fns. `cube(3)` finds `3` in cache from sq(3) → returns 9. Bug fix: put the Map inside memo() so each fn gets its own.

options.text: Iterable values (arrays, strings, Maps, Sets, generators)

questions.explanation: `for...of` needs the `[Symbol.iterator]` protocol. Plain objects don't have it — use `for...in` or `Object.entries` for those.
Promise.race settles with the first to settle — success OR failure. Rejection at 50ms wins over resolution at 100ms.

questions.prompt: Write a function `debounce(fn, wait)` that returns a debounced version of `fn`.
Write a function `throttle(fn, wait)` that ensures `fn` runs at most once per `wait` ms.
Write `deepClone(obj)` that handles nested objects, arrays, Dates, and cyclic references.

questions.explanation: `[] + []` → both to primitive → '' + '' = ''. `[] + {}` → '' + '[object Object]'. `{} + []` in a statement-position is parsed as an empty block + `+[]` = 0 in the REPL but same as the second in expression context. Both work as answer (a) in modern engines under expression evaluation.

options.text: Generational mark-and-sweep with young generation (scavenger) + old generation (major GC)

questions.explanation: Orinoco/Oilpan use generational + incremental. Long-lived objects promoted to old gen. Weakmaps and WeakRefs interoperate with GC.

questions.prompt: Which is a COMMON JS memory-leak source?

options.text: Growing Map/Array cache with no eviction, keyed by user

questions.explanation: Also: forgotten setInterval, DOM node references from JS after node removal, unremoved event listeners, closures capturing large arrays.

options.text: Object references only; entries are GC'd when the key object has no other strong references

questions.explanation: Useful for private state associated with an object without preventing GC. Not enumerable.
Later spreads overwrite earlier keys — `y` becomes 20.

options.text: `#field` syntax — truly runtime-private (unreachable from outside the class)

questions.explanation: TS `private` is compile-time only. `#field` enforces at runtime. Static private (`static #x`) also supported.

questions.prompt: What does this print, in order?
questions.explanation: Promise executor is SYNC — logs A immediately. Then B (sync). Then microtask flushes → C.

questions.code:
async function f() { return 1; }
f().then(v => console.log(v));
questions.explanation: async functions always return a Promise. Returning a non-Promise wraps it. `.then` unwraps.

options.text: The first one settles (success or failure)
The first one FULFILLS; rejects with AggregateError only if all reject

questions.explanation: any = first success. race = first settle. all = all success or one reject. allSettled = wait for all outcomes.
allSettled waits for all, returns {status, value|reason} — never rejects.
Array.from with array-like + map function is the canonical range helper.

questions.code:
const a = [3, 1, 2, 10, 5];
console.log(a.sort());
questions.explanation: Default sort compares as STRINGS lexicographically. Always pass `(a,b) => a - b` for numeric sort.

options.text: Not defined; use `import.meta.dirname` (Node 20+) or derive from `import.meta.url`

questions.explanation: ESM removed __dirname/__filename. Node 20+ shipped `import.meta.dirname` and `import.meta.filename` as replacements.
Set constructor accepts any iterable; generators are iterable.

options.text: Nested objects/arrays, Dates, RegExps, Maps, Sets, TypedArrays, cyclic refs; does NOT clone functions or DOM nodes

questions.explanation: Built-in structured cloning is the modern deep-clone. Native in Node 17+, all modern browsers.

questions.code:
const it = [1, 2, 3][Symbol.iterator]();
console.log(it.next().value, it.next().value);
questions.explanation: Arrays expose Symbol.iterator — the iterator protocol under `for...of`.

options.text: Unique property keys that don't collide with string keys — used for meta/well-known protocols (Symbol.iterator, Symbol.asyncIterator)

questions.explanation: Symbols are unique + non-enumerable via Object.keys → great for extending built-ins safely.

options.text: Intercept fundamental object operations — used by Vue reactivity, ORM lazy-loading, negative-array indexing

questions.explanation: Reactivity systems + observability libraries lean on Proxy heavily. Cost: no equality via ===, some perf overhead.
Async generators + for-await-of are the streaming primitive for pull-based async data.

options.text: Cancel fetch/setTimeout/user code by passing its `signal` and listening for 'abort'

questions.explanation: Standard cancellation primitive. Node's `setTimeout({ signal })` and fetch both accept it.

questions.code: const r = [[1,2],[3,4],[5]].reduce((a, b) => a.concat(b), []);
questions.explanation: Classic flatten. Modern: `arr.flat()`. Deep: `arr.flat(Infinity)`.

questions.prompt: Which iterate ONLY own-enumerable string keys? (select all)
questions.explanation: for...in also enumerates inherited. getOwnPropertyNames includes non-enumerable. Reflect.ownKeys also includes Symbols.

questions.prompt: In an ESM module, top-level `await` is:

options.text: Allowed — the module becomes async, importing modules wait for it before running

questions.explanation: Great for boot-time config fetches / dynamic imports. Loading is still parallel across independent modules.

options.text: Using the same regex INSTANCE across multiple `.exec()` or `.test()` calls — state persists between calls

questions.explanation: Global regexes carry lastIndex. Subtle bug when a regex is reused in a loop. `matchAll` avoids this — returns an iterator.

questions.code: console.log('hello'.padStart(8, '*'));
questions.explanation: padStart adds to the front; padEnd to the back. Great for CLI table formatting.

options.text: Indistinguishable from MAX_SAFE_INTEGER + 2 in Number — use BigInt for integer precision beyond 2^53-1

questions.explanation: IEEE 754 doubles carry ~15-16 significant digits. BigInt has arbitrary precision but is not interoperable with Number arithmetic.

questions.prompt: In the browser, transferring data to a Web Worker via `postMessage(buf, [buf])`:

options.text: Transfers ownership — buf is neutered in the sender; zero-copy

questions.explanation: Transferable objects (ArrayBuffer, MessagePort, etc.) skip the structured-clone copy for large payloads.

options.text: Waits for a and c to finish then rejects
Rejects immediately with b's reason; a and c continue running but their results are discarded

questions.explanation: For fail-fast semantics use all; for wait-all use allSettled. Discarded promises may still cause 'unhandledRejection'.

questions.prompt: Write `promiseAllLimit(promises, limit)` — like Promise.all but with concurrency limit.
Write `once(fn)` — returns a function that runs `fn` at most once, cached-forever result.
